title: App API functions run in iad1 (US East) while the database is in ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)
rootCause: apps/app/vercel.json has no "regions" key, so Vercel runs every serverless function in the default iad1. Supabase prod (zdnypksjqnhtiblwdaic) and staging are in ap-southeast-1. apps/nexus/vercel.json:5 already pins regions ["sin1"]; the student app never got the same setting.
evidence: curl from India: x-vercel-id: bom1::iad1::... on /api/auth/health and /api/tools/exam-centers?action=states. Uncached /api/tools/exam-centers?action=states took ttfb 1.41s (MISS); the same URL from the edge cache took 0.18s (HIT). Every DB query from a function therefore crosses US East to Singapore (about 220ms RTT each way pair), and register-user runs about 7 to 9 sequential queries.
impact: Every authenticated hard load waits on POST /api/auth/register-user before the shell renders (see LOAD-2 finding), so roughly 1.5 to 2.5s of pure trans-Pacific latency sits on the critical path of every tool page. Every other app API (tools, notifications, heartbeat, devices, diagnostics) pays the same per-query penalty. Users are in India (edge bom1).
fix: Add "regions": ["sin1"] to apps/app/vercel.json (same as nexus), redeploy, and confirm x-vercel-id shows ::sin1::. Optionally bom1 if Vercel offers it on the plan, but sin1 is co-located with the DB which matters more because routes make many sequential queries.
risk: Low. Config-only. Cron jobs (none in apps/app/vercel.json) and env vars are unaffected. Verify Razorpay/Firebase Admin calls still work (they are global APIs).
expected: Uncached DB-backed API ttfb from India drops from about 1.4s to about 0.3 to 0.5s; register-user drops by roughly 1.5s.

title: Whole shell and page content blocked behind POST /api/auth/register-user on every hard load
rootCause: ProtectedLayoutInner renders a full-screen loader while (loading || (checkingUser && !!user) || sso.processing). checkingUser only flips after register-user resolves (layout.tsx:101-155). register-user (apps/app/src/app/api/auth/register-user/route.ts:31-238) runs verifyIdToken, insertFunnelEvent(register_user_started), getOrCreateUserFromFirebase, linkAnonymousEvents, insertFunnelEvent(register_user_completed), updateUser(last_login_at), optional student_profiles + lead_profiles lookups, and isEnrolledStudent, all awaited in sequence. Three of those are analytics or bookkeeping writes the screen does not need.
evidence: Critical path on a hard load: HTML (only the Suspense fallback, measured: prod HTML for /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator contains only 'Loading...' inside a BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING template) -> about 450 kB gz JS (measured) -> hydrate -> import('./firebase') + setPersistence + onAuthStateChanged (IndexedDB) -> getIdToken (network if older than 1h) -> POST register-user (7 to 9 sequential DB round trips, iad1 to Singapore) -> shell + page render -> page fetches. Page data is 4 serial hops after JS. The in-flight redesign swaps the text for AppSplash but keeps the same gate.
impact: Every PWA launch, refresh or deep link shows a blocking splash for the full register-user duration (estimated 1.5 to 3s with the region mismatch, not measured end to end because the Entra/Firebase login wall blocks automated runs). The phone-verify and onboarding gates are the only consumers that truly need the response. Also writes 2 funnel_events rows and a users.last_login_at update per hard load.
fix: 1) Render AppShell + children as soon as the Firebase user is known; run register-user in the background and gate only the phone modal, onboarding wizard, install banner and report FAB on its result. 2) Cache the last register-user payload in sessionStorage keyed by uid and paint from it, revalidating in the background (render it after mount to stay hydration safe). 3) In the route, move insertFunnelEvent, linkAnonymousEvents and updateUser(last_login_at) off the response path (Promise.all or waitUntil/after()), and parallelise the student_profiles, lead_profiles and isEnrolledStudent lookups with Promise.all. 4) Consider calling it once per session (sessionStorage flag) rather than per hard load.
risk: Medium. Pages that read supabaseUser-derived props (accountTier, phoneVerified) must tolerate a pending value; the phone modal must not flash for verified users (keep it hidden until the response or cache says unverified).
expected: Shell and tool content visible right after Firebase resolves (about 0.3 to 0.8s after hydration instead of 2 to 3s); one fewer serial hop for page data.

title: NeramThemeProvider uses one module-level Emotion cache on the server, so prerendered and warm-instance HTML ships without its MUI CSS
rootCause: const clientSideEmotionCache = createEmotionCache() is created at module scope and passed to CacheProvider on the server too (provider.tsx:143,223). @emotion/cache 11.14 server insert sets cache.inserted[name] = true and @emotion/utils only emits SSR <style> tags for names not yet in cache.inserted. So once one render (one prerendered page in the build worker, or one request on a warm lambda) has emitted a class, every later render in that process omits its CSS. There is no useServerInsertedHTML flush (ThemeRegistry.tsx has one, but the app does not use it).
evidence: Fetched prod HTML and compared class names used vs <style data-emotion> defined: /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator used 2 neram-mui classes, defined 0 (the centring Box neram-mui-ue6sde and the Typography have no CSS); /privacy-policy used 12, missing 4; / and /login complete. The cutoff page carries only the CssBaseline global style.
impact: Every protected route (all tools) first paints the loader unstyled, top-left, then jumps when JS inserts CSS: a flash and a layout shift on every hard load. Public static pages render partly unstyled until hydration. Affects every app that uses NeramThemeProvider for SSR (marketing too).
fix: Create the cache per render on the server: in NeramThemeProvider use useState(() => createEmotionCache()) and flush inserted names with useServerInsertedHTML (the pattern already in packages/ui/src/theme/ThemeRegistry.tsx), or wrap with @mui/material-nextjs AppRouterCacheProvider. Keep the module-level cache only for the browser.
risk: Medium. Shared package change rebuilds all four apps; test hard loads of marketing and app pages for duplicate style tags and FOUC.
expected: Every SSR/prerendered page ships the CSS for every class it uses (used minus defined = 0 on all pages).

history.note: NeramThemeProvider: per-render server Emotion cache flushed via useServerInsertedHTML (compat mode); browser keeps one shared cache; nested providers reuse the outer cache. Local prod build: used-minus-defined classes 0 on 8 pages, repeat requests too (prod before: 91 of 92 missing on college predictor).

title: Service worker is generated but never registered (next-pwa 5 does not inject registration for the App Router)
rootCause: next-pwa 5.6 (register: true) injects its register script into the pages-router main entry. The app is App Router only (main-app entry), and nothing in src calls navigator.serviceWorker.register. Same failure the Nexus notes record for its next-pwa setup.
evidence: Downloaded every script chunk referenced by prod / and /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator (23 chunks): zero contain navigator.serviceWorker.register or the string /sw.js. The only serviceWorker references are Firebase Auth internals. Prod /sw.js exists (117 precache entries, about 2.47 MB transfer) but no page registers it.
impact: No offline support, no asset caching, for an app advertised and installed as a PWA (manifest display standalone, shortcuts). On browsers that still require a service worker for installability, beforeinstallprompt never fires so InstallPromptBanner never shows. The committed apps/app/public/sw.js and workbox-*.js are dead artefacts that churn on every local build (they are also listed in .gitignore but tracked).
fix: Decide deliberately. If offline is wanted, register explicitly from a small client component in the root layout (navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js') after load), and before enabling it fix the latent issues: drop the default runtime caching for /api/ (see the redacted finding), add ChunkLoadError recovery (reload once), and prefer a prompt-to-update flow over skipWaiting+clientsClaim. If not wanted, remove next-pwa, untrack public/sw.js and workbox-*.js, and keep the manifest only (as Nexus did with a hand-written nexus-sw.js).
risk: Turning registration on changes caching for every user at once; ship behind a kill switch (an unregister script) and test a deploy-while-open scenario.
expected: Either a working, deliberately scoped service worker or no generated SW artefacts at all.

title: Latent service worker caching concern (details in report)
Theme mode read from localStorage in a useState initializer (hydration mismatch for dark and system users)
rootCause: useState(() => getInitialMode(storageKey, defaultMode)) returns defaultMode ('light') on the server and the stored value on the client. actualMode for 'system' also calls matchMedia in useMemo (provider.tsx:179-184). The selected MUI theme therefore differs between server and first client render.
evidence: AppSidebar exposes a dark mode toggle that writes neram-theme-mode. Palette-dependent sx produces different Emotion class names per theme, so any server-rendered MUI element whose styles read the palette mismatches. In apps/app the protected subtree bails out to client rendering (useSearchParams in useSSOToken), which shields tool pages, but the root providers, /login, /, /privacy-policy and other public pages hydrate. Not reproduced with the dev overlay in this audit.
impact: Dark-mode users get React #418/#423 on public pages and the login screen, which re-renders the whole root (all providers remount, effects restart). Also a light flash before dark applies.
fix: Initialise mode to defaultMode, read localStorage in an effect (or behind a mounted flag), and to avoid the flash use MUI CssVarsProvider with getInitColorSchemeScript (or a tiny inline script that sets data-mui-color-scheme before paint).
risk: Low to medium; shared package, all apps rebuild. A brief light-to-dark switch appears if only the effect fix is done.
expected: Zero hydration warnings on a hard load with neram-theme-mode=dark.

history.note: Mode starts at defaultMode on server and first client render; stored mode and OS preference applied after mount; system mode now follows OS changes. Playwright: 0 hydration errors light/dark/system at 375 and 1280. provider.test.tsx added.

title: Production MUI text never uses the downloaded webfonts; Inter and DM Sans are both preloaded
rootCause: HEAD loads Inter and DM_Sans via next/font with variables, but the committed theme (apps/app/src/lib/theme.ts at HEAD, typography.fontFamily) used the literal '"DM Sans", "Inter", system-ui'. next/font registers the families as __DM_Sans_0eeb07 and __Inter_8b3a0b, so the literals never match. body gets inter.className (Inter) which only reaches raw text outside MUI.
evidence: Prod CSS 5e7639537dff7a20.css: font-family:__Inter_8b3a0b (28 faces) and __DM_Sans_0eeb07 (8 faces). Prod CssBaseline style: body{font-family:"DM Sans","Inter",system-ui,...}. Two preloads on every page: 13971731025ec697-s.p.woff2 (36,980 B) and e4af272ccee01ff0-s.p.woff2 (48,432 B). The layout also preconnects to fonts.gstatic.com and dns-prefetches fonts.googleapis.com, which next/font never uses, and emits the manifest link twice (metadata.manifest plus a manual <link>).
impact: About 85 kB of font downloads per cold visit while all MUI Typography and Buttons render in system-ui; one wasted cross-origin connection per page.
fix: The in-flight working copy already drops Inter, sets display swap and points the theme at var(--font-dm-sans) (theme.ts:19-20). Before committing: also remove the Google Fonts preconnect/dns-prefetch and the duplicate <link rel=manifest> (layout.tsx:79,82-83), and check that CssBaseline body font-family resolves to __DM_Sans in prod HTML.
risk: Low. Visual change: text switches from system-ui to DM Sans.
expected: One font family preloaded, MUI text renders in DM Sans, no Google Fonts preconnect.

title: Firebase ID token captured once at login and reused for heartbeat, diagnostics, error logs, funnel events and onboarding after it expires
rootCause: setIdToken(idToken) and setFunnelTrackerToken(idToken) store the token string from the first register-user call. It is never refreshed. useActiveTimeTracker (hooks/useActiveTimeTracker.ts:147), GlobalErrorLogger (components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:29), diagnostics (layout.tsx:175), OnboardingWizard (userToken prop) and funnel-tracker.ts:236 all send it in the body. Server verifyIdToken (apps/app/src/lib/firebase-admin.ts:58) rejects expired tokens; heartbeat returns 401 (api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:49-51).
evidence: Firebase ID tokens live 60 minutes. No code path calls getIdToken() again for these consumers.
impact: After an hour on one page: a 401 heartbeat every 60s for the rest of the session (each a billed function call), crash logs silently lost (the error logger is useless exactly when long sessions misbehave), funnel events rejected or attributed anonymously, and an onboarding wizard left open over an hour fails to save.
fix: Pass a getToken function (getFirebaseAuth().currentUser?.getIdToken()) instead of a token string, so the SDK refreshes as needed; in funnel-tracker resolve the token at flush time. Stop the heartbeat on a 401 instead of retrying every minute.
expected: No 401s from heartbeat/diagnostics/funnel-events in a 2-hour session.

title: Heartbeat poller keeps firing in hidden tabs, has no backoff, and calls geolocation every minute
rootCause: setInterval(sendHeartbeat, 60000) is never paused on visibilitychange. The 1s tick keeps adding idleSeconds while hidden, so active===0 && idle===0 is never true and a POST /api/devices/heartbeat goes out every minute (subject to browser timer throttling). Each beat first awaits navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition. No in-flight guard, no backoff after 401/5xx. The effect also re-runs when diagnosticSessionId arrives, and the cleanup sends an extra heartbeat.
evidence: Poller table: interval 60s; pauses when hidden: no (only sends a beacon on hide); backoff: no; single instance: yes; skips when in flight: no; stops on sign-out: yes (layout unmount). Combined with the stale token finding, a tab left open overnight sends hundreds of 401s.
impact: Function invocations and DB writes from tabs nobody is looking at; battery and location use on phones.
fix: Use the existing useVisibilityPolling from @neram/ui (or stop/start the interval on visibilitychange), stop counting idle while hidden, drop geolocation from the heartbeat (or read it at most once per session), and stop after a 401.
risk: Low; active-time totals for hidden tabs drop, which is the correct behaviour.
expected: Zero heartbeat requests while document.visibilityState is hidden.

title: Location permission requested automatically (high accuracy) after login and in every heartbeat
rootCause: collectLocation() calls getCurrentPosition with enableHighAccuracy: true from the protected layout's diagnostics effect (layout.tsx:168) once per session, with no user gesture and no explanation; useActiveTimeTracker.ts:132 calls it again every 60s.
evidence: Static read. Browsers show (or quietly suppress) a location prompt on the first protected page after sign-in, on top of the phone verification modal. The diagnostics POST awaits it, so if the prompt is ignored the session row is never written.
impact: A permission prompt the student did not ask for on first use (a trust and conversion cost on the most important screen), GPS battery use on phones, and a privacy question about storing precise location for a tools app.
fix: Do not request location automatically. If location is needed (exam centre distance), ask in that tool with context, and use coarse data (timezone, IP country) for diagnostics. Send the diagnostics session without waiting for geolocation.
risk: Low; product owner should confirm whether precise location is used anywhere.
expected: No geolocation prompt unless the student taps a location feature.

title: No global-error.tsx or not-found.tsx; errors in the protected layout itself have no boundary; ChunkLoadError not handled
rootCause: (protected)/error.tsx exists and has reset, but an error.tsx does not catch errors thrown by the layout of its own segment. ProtectedLayoutInner renders AppShell, both AppSidebars, three bells, LoginModal, OnboardingWizard, InstallPromptBanner and ReportProblemFab; a throw in any of them goes to the root, which has no error.tsx and no global-error.tsx. There is no app/not-found.tsx. error.tsx does not special-case ChunkLoadError, so 'Try again' (reset) re-renders without fetching the missing chunk.
evidence: GET https://app.neramclasses.com/this-does-not-exist-xyz returns Next's default unbranded '404: This page could not be found.' page with no navigation back. ls apps/app/src/app shows only layout.tsx and page.tsx at the root.
impact: A shell bug becomes Next's white 'Application error: a client-side exception has occurred' screen with no way back except reload. Students who mistype or follow an old link get a dead end. After a deploy, a stale tab that lazy-loads a chunk shows the error screen and 'Try again' cannot fix it.
fix: Add app/global-error.tsx (minimal, own <html><body>, reload button), app/not-found.tsx (branded, link to /dashboard and /tools/all), and either app/error.tsx or move the shell under a child segment so (protected)/error.tsx sits below it. In error.tsx, if error.name === 'ChunkLoadError' or message matches /Loading chunk|Failed to fetch dynamically imported module/, do a one-time window.location.reload() guarded by sessionStorage.
expected: A thrown error in AppSidebar leaves a branded recoverable screen; unknown URLs show a branded 404 with a way back.

title: @neram/auth barrel ships MSAL and server-side Graph code to the student app; the dynamic import of firebase does not split
rootCause: index.ts statically re-exports ./firebase, ./microsoft (@azure/msal-browser) and ./graph (865 lines of server-only Graph calls). The package has no sideEffects flag, so every `import { useFirebaseAuth } from '@neram/auth'` pulls all three into the client graph. hooks.tsx uses await import('./firebase') for code splitting, but index.ts already imports ./firebase statically, so it splits nothing. Also package.json exports './hooks' points at ./src/hooks.ts, which does not exist (the file is hooks.tsx).
evidence: Prod chunk 1973-b1f362c41d7ad752.js (295,423 B raw, 74,197 B gz) on /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator contains PublicClientApplication and BrowserAuthError (MSAL). Measured first-load JS for that route: about 1.71 MB raw, 490 kB gz including 39 kB of nomodule polyfills.
impact: Students on phones download and parse Microsoft auth code they never use on every cold load. Graph helpers read non-public env names, so nothing secret leaks, but the code is shipped.
fix: Add subpath entry points and use them from apps/app: @neram/auth/firebase and a Firebase-only hooks entry; mark the package "sideEffects": false; fix the './hooks' export to ./src/hooks.tsx. Move graph.ts behind a server-only subpath (@neram/auth/graph with import 'server-only').
risk: Medium: shared package change fans out to all four apps; Nexus and Admin must import MSAL from the new subpath.
expected: No MSAL symbols in any apps/app client chunk; tool route first-load JS down by an estimated 40 to 60 kB gz (not measured).

history.note: @neram/auth sideEffects:false, ./hooks export fixed to hooks.tsx, ./graph subpath added, optimizePackageImports in apps/app. No MSAL symbols in any apps/app route chunk after build.

title: @neram/ui root barrel has no sideEffects flag, so the tools route ships ChatWidget and other unused components
rootCause: packages/ui/package.json has no "sideEffects": false; index.ts is 'use client' and re-exports theme, every component (ChatWidget, ConnectToOffice, LoginModal, DocumentUpload, ImageUpload*), hooks and a long icon list. The app imports Box/Typography/Button and LoginModal from the root barrel in the shell.
evidence: Prod chunk 9086-2caf4af53c760dd2.js (120,500 B raw, 32,303 B gz) on the cutoff calculator route contains ChatWidget and ConnectToOffice strings; chunk 6449 (410 kB raw, 111 kB gz) is MUI core. Total first-load JS for the route about 450 kB gz (excluding polyfills), above the 300 kB guide.
impact: Slower first load and parse on the low-end Android phones most students use.
fix: Add "sideEffects": ["*.css"] or false to packages/ui/package.json, verify with a build of apps/app, and lazy-load LoginModal in the protected layout via next/dynamic (it is only shown to phone-unverified users).
risk: Medium: verify no module in @neram/ui relies on import-time side effects.
expected: ChatWidget absent from tool route chunks; first-load JS reduced (not measured).

history.note: @neram/ui sideEffects:false, ./components export fixed, optimizePackageImports ['@neram/ui','@neram/auth'] in apps/app (the 'use client' root barrel otherwise ships every export), LoginModal lazy-loaded in StudentSession. Tool routes 367-369 kB to 229-232 kB first load; / 399 to 254 kB; ChatWidget absent.

title: Each useFirebaseAuth call is an independent subscription starting at loading:true, so AuthGate flashes a spinner on every tool mount
rootCause: useFirebaseAuth keeps its own useState({loading:true}) and its own onAuthStateChanged subscription. On a tool page there are about 5 instances (protected layout, PendingEnrollmentBanner, the page, AuthGate x1 or x2, useScoreAutoSave). AuthGate.tsx:61-75 renders a 200px Paper with a spinner while its own instance is loading, even though the protected layout already guarantees a signed-in user.
evidence: Static read. Inside (protected), AuthGate's signed-out branch, the emoji gate copy (AuthGate.tsx:96,134-136) and ToolAuthModal can never render because the layout redirects anonymous users to /login, yet ToolAuthModal is imported statically on 8 tool pages.
impact: A 200px spinner box appears and collapses on every soft navigation to a tool that uses AuthGate (layout shift), dead code in every tool bundle, and redundant auth subscriptions.
fix: Provide auth once (the existing AuthProvider in hooks.tsx, or a context set by the protected layout) and read it with useContext so new mounts see the current user immediately. Inside (protected), drop AuthGate or make it render children directly when the layout's user exists; lazy-load ToolAuthModal if public tools come back.
risk: Low to medium; check public pages that may rely on AuthGate's signed-out branch.
expected: No spinner flash when moving between tool pages; one onAuthStateChanged subscription per app.

title: InstallPromptBanner attaches its beforeinstallprompt listener too late and misses the event
rootCause: InstallPromptBanner (and its useInstallPrompt listener, hooks/useInstallPrompt.ts:119) only mounts after register-user returns with phoneVerified && onboardingCompleted. Chrome fires beforeinstallprompt once, early in the page lifetime; if it fires during the auth splash nobody calls preventDefault or stores it.
evidence: Static ordering: Firebase init + register-user (seconds) precede the listener. Also see the service worker finding: on browsers that require a SW for installability the event never fires at all.
impact: The custom install prompt rarely or never appears on hard loads, so the PWA install funnel underperforms.
fix: Capture beforeinstallprompt at app start in a tiny module or root-layout client component (store the event in a module variable), and have InstallPromptBanner read the stored event when it mounts.
expected: Banner appears for eligible users on the first qualifying load.

title: /tools/nata/college-predictor is a client-side redirect that waits for full sign-in, and it is the PWA shortcut target
rootCause: page.tsx only calls redirect('/tools/counseling/college-predictor'), but it sits under the client protected layout whose subtree bails out to client rendering, so the redirect is serialised into the RSC payload and only runs after Firebase auth and register-user complete. The layout still publishes title, description and a canonical for the redirecting URL. manifest.json shortcut 'College Predictor' and next.config.js redirect /tools/college-predictor point at this URL.
evidence: curl: /tools/nata/college-predictor returns 200 (x-vercel-cache HIT) with 'NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/tools/counseling/college-predictor;307;' in the payload and title 'NATA College Predictor 2026 ... | Neram | aiArchitek by Neram Classes'. /tools/college-predictor returns 308 to it, making a 2-hop chain.
impact: Launching the 'College Predictor' shortcut from the home screen shows the auth splash, then the shell, then navigates again. Search engines see a 200 page whose canonical points to itself but whose content is a redirect.
fix: Add { source: '/tools/nata/college-predictor', destination: '/tools/counseling/college-predictor', permanent: true } to next.config.js redirects, point the /tools/college-predictor redirect and the manifest shortcut straight at /tools/counseling/college-predictor, and delete this layout and page.
expected: Single 308 at the edge; shortcut opens the predictor directly.

title: Tool layouts publish SEO metadata for pages whose server HTML is only a loader
rootCause: The metadata-only server layouts are fine on their own, but every page below (protected) is client rendered behind the auth gate, so crawlers receive title, description and canonical with an empty body. exam-centers/layout.tsx:4-20 still says 2025. Titles also get the root template appended ('... | Neram | aiArchitek by Neram Classes', 'Help & Support | NATA Tools - Neram Classes | aiArchitek by Neram Classes').
evidence: Prod HTML for /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator and /tools/help contains only 'Loading...' in the body (help shows 'Help & Support' only in head tags).
impact: No ranking value from these canonical URLs; soft-404 risk. Not a runtime cost.
fix: SEO owner decision: either serve a public, server-rendered summary for tool pages (outside the auth gate) or mark them noindex and keep the SEO pages on marketing. Update the 2025 copy and use title.absolute or drop '| Neram' from the per-page titles.
expected: Indexed tool URLs carry real content, or are explicitly noindex.

title: Help page loads Tawk.to per mount with incomplete cleanup, links to redirecting legacy URLs, and uses emoji icons
rootCause: The effect appends embed.tawk.to script on mount; cleanup removes only the <script> and deletes window.Tawk_API, but Tawk's injected iframes and widget DOM stay. Returning to /tools/help injects a second script with a fresh Tawk_API. faqTopics hrefs (help/page.tsx:12-27) use /tools/cutoff-calculator etc., which 308 to /tools/nata/*. Topic icons are emoji, against the repo rule of SVG icons.
evidence: Static read; Tawk env vars presence in prod not checked.
impact: Duplicate or orphaned chat widgets after soft navigation, an extra redirect per click, inconsistent iconography.
fix: Load Tawk once per app (module-level guard, or next/script with lazyOnload and an id) and hide/show via Tawk_API.hideWidget/showWidget on route change; link directly to /tools/nata/* and /tools/counseling/*; swap emoji for MUI SVG icons.
expected: One widget instance regardless of navigation; no redirect hops from help links.

title: Sidebar exam tab initialised once from pathname (HEAD); bottom nav uses router.push without prefetch and a hard-coded Tools target
rootCause: HEAD: useState(() => pathname.startsWith('/tools/counseling') ? 2 : ...) never re-syncs, and both AppSidebar instances persist across navigations, so opening a JEE or Counseling tool from the dashboard leaves the NATA list showing with no active item. HEAD MobileBottomNav.tsx:86 navigates via router.push in BottomNavigation onChange (no <a href>, no prefetch, no open-in-new-tab), Tools pointed at /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator, and value falls back to 0 so Home looks active on /profile-like routes outside the five tabs.
evidence: The in-flight working copy fixes all three: AppSidebar now derives track from the route with a useEffect, MobileBottomNav renders next/link items with aria-current, and Tools points to TOOLS_HOME_HREF '/tools/all' with isNavActive.
impact: Production (HEAD) users see the wrong tool list and a slower tab switch; resolved once the redesign ships.
fix: Ship the working-copy changes; add a Playwright mobile test that taps each bottom tab and checks aria-current, and a desktop test that opens /tools/jee/* and checks the JEE list is shown.
expected: Sidebar list and bottom-tab highlight always match the current route after soft navigation.

title: Full-screen plain-text 'Loading...' states with no branding, status role or skeleton (HEAD)
rootCause: HEAD renders <Typography>Loading...</Typography> for the Suspense fallback and for the auth/register gate, and returns null (blank) while redirecting signed-out users (layout.tsx:356).
evidence: Prod HTML for every tools route is that fallback, and its Box/Typography CSS is missing from the SSR HTML (see the Emotion cache finding), so it first paints top-left unstyled. The working copy replaces both with AppSplash (role=status, aria-busy, brand mark); the blocking gate itself remains (see LOAD-2 HIGH).
impact: Unbranded, unannounced wait on every hard load in production.
fix: Ship AppSplash; also render it (instead of null) during the signed-out redirect, and make sure its styles are present in SSR HTML once the Emotion fix lands.
expected: Branded splash, announced to screen readers, styled on first paint.

title: Pending enrollment banner refetched on every hard load and inserted above content after paint
rootCause: GET /api/enrollment/pending runs once per AppShell mount (each hard load) unless dismissed; res.json() is called without checking res.ok; the Alert is inserted above {children}, pushing the page down when it resolves. It also opens its own useFirebaseAuth subscription.
evidence: Static read.
impact: One function call per hard load for a rare state, and a layout shift when it appears.
fix: Return pending enrollment inside the register-user payload (already fetched per hard load) or cache the result in sessionStorage; check res.ok; reserve space or render it as a non-shifting toast/snackbar.
expected: Zero extra request per hard load; no CLS from the banner.

title: Notification count poller has no error backoff (otherwise well disciplined)
rootCause: Shared poller (one per apiBaseUrl) pauses when hidden, skips when in flight, aborts at 15s and stops when the last bell unmounts, but on 401/5xx it keeps polling at the same 60s interval.
evidence: apps/app mounts three bells (AppTopBar, mobile drawer AppSidebar with keepMounted, desktop AppSidebar); network still shows one poller. Poller table: 60s, pauses hidden yes, backoff no, single instance yes, in-flight skip yes, stops on sign-out yes.
impact: During an outage each open tab keeps paying one call per minute; minor.
fix: Double the interval (cap 10 minutes) after consecutive failures and reset on success; stop on 401 until the token changes.
expected: Failing endpoint is polled at a decaying rate.

title: Funnel tracker flush on hide uses plain fetch and a beforeunload listener
rootCause: flushEvents() on visibilitychange hidden and beforeunload uses fetch without keepalive; when the page is being unloaded the request is cancelled without rejecting, so the sendBeacon fallback in catch never runs. Response status is not checked, so 4xx (for example the stale-token case) silently drops the batch. The beforeunload listener can make the page ineligible for the back/forward cache in some browsers.
evidence: Static read.
impact: Lost analytics events at session end (tool_opened for quick visits), slower back navigation on affected browsers.
fix: When hidden, use navigator.sendBeacon first (or fetch with keepalive: true); listen to pagehide instead of beforeunload; resolve the token at flush time.
expected: Events queued before tab close reach /api/funnel-events.

title: Global error logger posts every error with no rate limit and duplicates the error-buffer listeners
rootCause: Each window error or unhandled rejection triggers a POST /api/diagnostics; an error thrown in a loop (animation frame, poll) becomes a request storm. installErrorCapture (lib/error-buffer.ts:175-184) registers a second pair of listeners and also wraps window.fetch and console.error globally. Logging only starts after register-user succeeds, so boot errors are never sent.
evidence: Static read.
impact: Potential burst of function calls from one broken client; boot-time crashes invisible.
fix: Dedupe by message+stack and cap to a few posts per minute per session; install capture at root-layout level and send buffered entries once a token exists.
expected: At most N error posts per minute per tab; boot errors captured.

title: Invalid nesting in the notification popover (div inside p)
rootCause:
ListItemText secondary renders a Typography

; the secondary content is a (div) with caption Typography children. The primary Typography body2 (p) is also nested in ListItemText's primary span.
evidence: Client-only (popover opens after a click), so it produces validateDOMNesting warnings rather than hydration failures.
impact: Console noise that the error buffer captures into problem reports; invalid HTML.
fix: Pass secondaryTypographyProps={{ component: 'div' }} and primaryTypographyProps={{ component: 'div' }}, or use Box components directly.
expected: No validateDOMNesting warnings when opening the bell.

title: SidebarContext value and toggle recreated every render
rootCause: value={{ collapsed, toggleSidebar, sidebarWidth }} and toggleSidebar are new objects per render. Consumers are few (AppShell, two AppSidebars) and the provider only re-renders on its own state, so the cost is small. localStorage is correctly read in an effect (no HYD-1 issue).
evidence: Static read.
impact: Negligible today; grows if more consumers subscribe.
fix: useCallback for toggleSidebar and useMemo for the value when touching this file next.
expected: Stable context value between collapse toggles.

title: No Web Vitals or server timing; TypeScript errors ignored at build; no app notes file
rootCause: No useReportWebVitals, @vercel/speed-insights or Server-Timing headers in apps/app. typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true lets type errors ship (the repo has a recorded prod white-screen that passed type-check). The perf-audit skill has nexus-notes.md but no app notes file (ARCH-1).
evidence: grep found no web-vitals reporting in apps/app; .claude/skills/perf-audit/ contains only nexus-notes.md.
impact: The next slowdown of the student app cannot be located without guessing; LCP/INP on phones is unknown.
fix: Add useReportWebVitals posting to an existing analytics endpoint (sampled), add Server-Timing to register-user, and create app-notes.md with the architecture map from this audit. Plan to remove ignoreBuildErrors once types are regenerated.
expected: LCP/INP/CLS per route visible; architecture notes exist.

title: Cloudflare overrides sw.js caching to 4 hours and the committed sw.js is stale
rootCause: vercel.json sets /sw.js to max-age=0, but the response passes through Cloudflare (Server: cloudflare) whose Browser Cache TTL rewrites it. apps/app/public/sw.js and workbox-ac6139fe.js are tracked in git despite .gitignore lines 61-64, and the committed copy references build OyL1g_YyrBKe57de3KCX8 while prod serves Hzv3hyar-ZHXxlBIqEk-I.
evidence: curl -I /sw.js: Cache-Control: public, max-age=14400, must-revalidate; cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED. /manifest.json keeps max-age=0.
impact: Dormant today because no page registers the SW; becomes relevant if registration is enabled (service worker script updates are usually fetched bypassing the HTTP cache, but intermediaries and imported scripts are not). Committed artefacts create noisy diffs that touch apps/app on every local build.
fix: Add a Cloudflare cache rule bypassing /sw.js and /workbox-*.js (or set Browser Cache TTL to respect origin), and git rm --cached the generated files.
expected: sw.js served with max-age=0 end to end; no generated SW files in commits.

title: Google Ads tag is a client component and the Ads ID is not configured in production
rootCause: GoogleAdsTag is 'use client' only to read a NEXT_PUBLIC env at build time; it uses next/script lazyOnload (good). Prod HTML has no googletagmanager reference, so NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_ADS_ID is unset and the signup conversion code in the protected layout (layout.tsx:133-141) never runs.
evidence: grep of prod /tools/nata/cutoff-calculator HTML: 0 googletagmanager matches.
impact: No cost today; signup conversions are not reported to Google Ads, which may not be intended.
fix: Confirm with marketing whether Ads tracking should be on for app.neramclasses.com; drop 'use client' (Script works in server components).
expected: Intentional state for Ads tracking.

title: Fixed bottom bars on tool pages sit under the shell's MobileBottomNav below 600px, hiding Save My Plan and the cutoff score bar
rootCause: Pages add their own position:fixed bottom:0 bars with zIndex 1100. MobileBottomNav (components/shell/MobileBottomNav.tsx:191) is also fixed bottom:0 with zIndex theme.zIndex.appBar (1100), 57px tall, shown at xs (<600px), and is rendered after <main> in AppShell, so at equal z-index it paints on top. The page bars do not offset by the nav height.
evidence: ExamPlannerContent.tsx:276-292 SelectionSummary Paper fixed bottom:0 zIndex 1100, about 73px tall; its small Save My Plan button sits about 20 to 52px from the bottom, fully under the 57px nav. cutoff-calculator/page.tsx:981-996 MobileStickyResult fixed bottom:0 zIndex 1100 (display xs to md), See Details button sits under the nav. question-bank/page.tsx:266-286 FAB bottom:24 zIndex 1000, lower 33px covered by the nav; it also touches ReportProblemFab (bottom 80, right 16) with no gap. AppShell.tsx:105 gives main pb 56px only.
impact: On phones (about 60% of users) the exam planner's only save action is unreachable, so plans cannot be saved; the cutoff sticky summary is mostly hidden; the QB FAB has half its tap area covered. Desktop: SelectionSummary left:0 spans under the sidebar.
fix: Offset page-level bottom bars by the nav: bottom: { xs: 'calc(56px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))', sm: 0 } and left: { sm: sidebarWidth }, or render them through a shared BottomActionBar slot in AppShell that stacks above MobileBottomNav. Move the QB FAB to bottom: { xs: 72 + 16 } and drop it (the header already has Post Question) or merge with ReportProblemFab spacing.
risk: Low. Layout-only change; verify at 375, 768 and 1280 with the nav, the Report FAB and iOS safe area.
expected: Save My Plan, See Details and the FAB fully visible and tappable above the bottom nav at 375px.

title: Question bank access gate can be bypassed client-side
AuthGate re-runs the page action after the first click: exam-centers search POSTs twice (double tool_completed log, double geolocation)
rootCause: AuthGate (components/AuthGate.tsx:44-52) calls onAuthenticated 100ms after it sees user && hasData for the first time. In (protected) the user is always signed in, so the first time hasData flips true (the user's own click) AuthGate fires the action a second time. searchCenters has no in-flight guard.
evidence: exam-centers/page.tsx:338 setHasSearched(true) then AuthGate hasData={hasSearched} onAuthenticated={searchCenters} -> second POST /api/tools/exam-centers, which calls logToolUsage (api/tools/exam-centers/route.ts:127) again, and re-requests geolocation when Location ON. eligibility-checker/page.tsx:477 and cost-calculator/page.tsx:338 re-run their pure calculators (an extra render only).
impact: Every first search costs two serverless invocations, double-counts tool_completed analytics, and can show results from the slower of the two calls.
fix: Remove AuthGate from pages under (protected) (the layout already guarantees a user). If it must stay, pass no onAuthenticated, or only call it when the user transitioned from null to signed-in inside the gate.
risk: Low. The gate's signed-out branch is unreachable in (protected).
expected: One POST and one tool_completed per search.

title: AuthGate is dead weight in (protected): own auth hook shows a spinner over results on every reveal, and ships ToolAuthModal
rootCause: AuthGate calls its own useFirebaseAuth (packages/auth/src/hooks.tsx:41, per-instance state, starts loading:true, dynamic-imports firebase and awaits persistence). While loading it renders a CircularProgress Paper (minHeight 200) instead of children. In eligibility and cost the gate mounts only when results appear, so each Check or Calculate shows a spinner flash before the result. Its signed-out UI (emoji lock, ToolAuthModal) can never show under the protected layout.
evidence: cost-calculator/page.tsx:335 wraps the entire result table; eligibility-checker/page.tsx:474 wraps the breakdown and mounts on hasChecked; cutoff page.tsx:1219 and 1327; exam-centers page.tsx:607. AuthGate.tsx:96 and 134-136 use emoji icons.
impact: Layout shift and a spinner flash on instant, client-side calculations; extra JS (AuthGate + ToolAuthModal 254 lines) on four routes.
fix: Delete AuthGate usage from these four pages (render children directly). Keep AuthGate only for public routes outside (protected).
expected: Results render in the same frame as the click with no spinner.

title: Pages use their own useFirebaseAuth, which starts signed-out: anonymous first fetches, refetch when the user resolves, and a 'Sign in required' flash
rootCause: useFirebaseAuth is a per-component hook with no shared context; every page instance starts with user:null, loading:true even though ProtectedLayout already has the user. Effects keyed on user run twice (null, then the user).
evidence: question-bank/new/page.tsx:57 renders 'Sign in required' + Sign In button until the hook resolves. question-bank/page.tsx:37-41 marks onboarding checked with user null, so fetchQuestions (line 94) fires an anonymous GET /api/questions, then a second authed GET when user resolves (deps line 128). question-bank/[id]/page.tsx:70-147 effect deps [id, user] fetch question+comments anonymously, then again with auth. useExamPlanner.ts:52-53 waits on its own hook before fetching.
impact: Extra requests on every QB visit, a visible signed-out flash on Post a Question, and a slower first data fetch on all four pages.
fix: Expose the layout's user/idToken through a context (or make useFirebaseAuth read a module-level store seeded by the first subscriber, initialised from auth.currentUser) and gate page fetches on that, so pages start with the signed-in user.
risk: Medium: touches pkg:@neram/auth or the app layout; all apps use the hook. An app-level context is the safer first step.
expected: One authed request per resource on mount; no signed-out flash.

title: Question detail: duplicate and racing fetches overwrite each other, and child components freeze the first (anonymous) data
rootCause: The fetch effect has no AbortController or cancelled flag, runs once anonymous and once authed, and both write question/comments/loading. VoteButton (VoteButton.tsx:23-24) and CommentSection (CommentSection.tsx:170) copy props into useState once and never resync.
evidence: Per visit: GET /api/questions/{id} x2, /comments x2, GET qb-stats, POST qb-stats, then sequential GET /api/auth/me (line 118) and GET /edit-request (line 129) after the Promise.all; about 8 requests where 4 would do. /api/auth/me is fetched only to learn the DB user id that ProtectedLayout already has from register-user. If the anonymous response renders first, VoteButton shows no user vote and CommentSection keeps the anonymous comment list.
impact: Wrong vote state (user taps up on an already-upvoted question and removes their vote), stale comments, a longer waterfall on phones.
fix: Fetch once with the token (see shared auth finding), add a cancelled flag or AbortController keyed on id, run me/edit-request inside the same Promise.all (or return author-ownership from GET /api/questions/{id}), and key VoteButton/CommentSection on question.id + a data version, or make them controlled.
expected: 4 parallel requests, one render with the user's real vote.

title: Question bank list: stale response can overwrite a newer filter, and filters/page are lost on Back
rootCause: fetchQuestions has no abort or request id; each category/sort/page tap starts a new request and whichever resolves last wins. category, sortBy and page are local state, not URL params.
evidence: page.tsx:94-128 setQuestions(data.data) unconditionally; page.tsx:18-21 local state; [id]/page.tsx:221-225 Back uses router.back, which remounts the list at page 1, All, Newest and refetches; scroll position is lost.
impact: Tapping Drawing then Mathematics quickly can show Drawing questions under the Mathematics chip. Browsing past page 1 is painful because every Back resets.
fix: Keep category/sort/page in searchParams (router.replace) and drive the fetch from them; ignore responses whose params differ from the latest (AbortController). Consider useSWR keyed on the URL so Back restores instantly from cache.
expected: The list always matches the selected chip; Back returns to the same page and filter.

title: Failed requests render as empty or not-found states with no retry
rootCause: Non-2xx and network errors are swallowed and the page falls through to its empty branch.
evidence: question-bank/page.tsx:118-125: non-ok leaves questions [] so the UI says 'No questions yet. Be the first to share'. question-bank/[id]/page.tsx:96-99 and 138-140: any error (offline, 500, 524) shows 'Question not found ... may have been removed'. useExamPlanner.ts:65-82: non-ok GET is silent, so a saved plan looks empty and can be overwritten. exam-centers/page.tsx:316-321 and 330-334: res.json() without res.ok, errors swallowed, the State select just shows All States; page.tsx:388-391 parses JSON before the ok check and returns silently on 401.
impact: Students on flaky mobile data see false 'no data' messages and have no way to retry except a full reload.
fix: Add an error state with a Retry button to each async region; check res.ok before res.json(); distinguish 404 from other failures on the detail page; on the planner, block editing until the GET succeeds.
expected: Every failure ends in a visible message with Retry.

title: Posting a comment that fails clears the typed text silently; comment vote ignores HTTP errors
rootCause: handleSubmitComment returns normally when the token is missing or res.ok is false, so handleTopLevelSubmit (line 197-205) and handleReply (line 47-56) clear the input as if it succeeded. handleVote (line 61-71) calls res.json() without res.ok and returns data.data (undefined on error).
evidence: CommentSection.tsx:173-195 and 197-205; CommentSection.tsx:61-71 feeds undefined into VoteButton's setScore/setUserVote.
impact: A student types a long answer on a phone, the POST fails, the text disappears with no error. Failed comment votes blank the score.
fix: Throw on !res.ok (and on missing token) so callers keep the text and show an inline error; check res.ok in handleVote and throw so VoteButton rolls back.
expected: Failed posts keep the draft and show 'Could not post, try again'.

title: Cutoff autosave writes a row on every 1.2s typing pause and pops the purpose bottom sheet over the results on phones
rootCause: Any change in resultData followed by a 1200ms pause POSTs /api/score-calculations, including partial numbers typed slowly on a phone. Responses are not ordered, so savedCalcId can end up pointing at an older calculation. Non-2xx saves keep lastSavedFingerprint, so they never retry. PurposePrompt opens a modal Drawer (mobileOpen defaults true) as soon as savedCalcId is set.
evidence: useScoreAutoSave.ts:79-131 (effect deps include a fresh resultData object every render, eslint-disable at 130), 115-119 (non-ok ignored), 133-154 (PATCH without res.ok). PurposePrompt.tsx:86 and 211-241; page.tsx:1243 mounts it on mobile step 3, where the save from step 2 already exists, so the sheet covers the results the moment the user arrives.
impact: Inflated score_calculations rows and 'You've calculated N times' counts, extra function invocations, a modal interrupting the result on 375px, purpose possibly attached to the wrong row.
fix: Save on explicit milestones (results first viewed, or blur/step change) rather than every pause; keep a request sequence number and ignore older responses; retry or surface non-2xx; on mobile show the purpose prompt inline below results (or after the user scrolls past them), not as an auto-opening modal.
risk: Low; analytics consumers of score_calculations may expect the current row volume.
expected: One saved row per completed calculation and no modal over results.

title: Cutoff What's Next buttons do a full page reload, re-running the whole protected-layout boot
rootCause: MUI Button with href and no component={Link} renders a plain <a>, so navigation is a document load.
evidence: page.tsx:944-960 Predict Your Rank and Find Colleges. A hard load shows ProtectedLayout's 'Loading...' text, re-inits Firebase, re-POSTs /api/auth/register-user and restarts device/heartbeat hooks before the next tool renders. The CTA also always suggests TNEA_BARCH whatever the board (page.tsx:941).
impact: Several seconds of 'Loading...' on mobile when moving to the next tool; lost SPA state.
fix: Add component={Link} to both Buttons; pick the counselling system from the board/state instead of hardcoding TNEA.
expected: Instant client-side transition.

title: On phones, results render below the form and info cards with no scroll or focus, after a 400px empty placeholder
rootCause: Desktop two-column Grid (inputs md=4/5, results md=7/8) stacks on xs with the secondary info card between the button and the results, and the empty results placeholder has minHeight 400.
evidence: eligibility-checker/page.tsx:371-385 (Key Requirements card) then 389-409 (minHeight 400 placeholder); cost-calculator/page.tsx:291-309 then 314-333; exam-centers/page.tsx:566-598 (legend + tips) then 602; image-crop/page.tsx:426-463 (spec card) then 467-576 (Download section). No scrollIntoView or focus move after the action.
impact: After tapping Check, Calculate, Search or Crop, nothing visibly changes in the viewport, so the tap feels dead; users must discover results by scrolling.
fix: Mobile-first order: inputs, primary button, then results; move reference cards below results (order prop or render after on xs); scroll results into view and move focus to the result heading on submit; drop the 400px placeholder on xs.
expected: Result appears in view within one tap at 375px.

title: Primary controls under 44px and text under 0.75rem across tool pages
rootCause: size='small' MUI controls (about 31 to 40px) and hard-coded fontSize 10/0.65rem/0.7rem chips and captions.
evidence: Under 44px: exam-centers page.tsx:233-240 'Show alternate center' (minHeight 0, px 0), 276-283 Get Directions, 484-494 Advanced Filters, 543-551 Use my location, small selects 437/455; cutoff page.tsx:366-375 and 513-522 small ToggleButtons, small TextFields 401-424, 1006 See Details; PurposePrompt.tsx:189-204 minHeight 36; image-crop page.tsx:331 Change Image; eligibility page.tsx:294-298 small checkboxes, 342/347 small radios; cost page.tsx:236/241 radios labelled '1'/'2', 482-490 Apply Now; ExamPlannerContent.tsx:305-325 Clear/Save small; question-bank CategoryFilter.tsx:190-197 chips minHeight 32, page.tsx:193-206 sort chips 24px, 243-261 pagination; [id] page.tsx:216-229 Back small, 286-301 IconButton small, VoteButton.tsx:72-123 32px. Under 0.75rem: exam-centers page.tsx:133, 149-201, 211, 244 (10 to 11px); AdminBadge.tsx:255 0.65rem; ImprovementSection.tsx:242-245 0.65rem; CommentSection.tsx:99,116 0.7rem; QuestionCard.tsx:105-151 0.7rem; ExamPlannerContent.tsx:185,189 0.7rem.
impact: Mis-taps and hard-to-read metadata on phones; fails the repo's 44 to 48px rule.
fix: Default tool forms to medium size with minHeight 48 on mobile (size={{ xs: 'medium' }} or sx minHeight), make filter chips 40px+ with 8px gaps, raise metadata text to 0.75rem minimum. Run /ui-ux-pro-max during the redesign.
risk: Low; denser desktop layouts can keep small sizes from md up.
expected: All tappables at least 44x44 at 375px.

title: QB 'not interested' path redirects to /tools/nata, which has no page (404 dead end); onboarding flags are not keyed per account
rootCause: There is no src/app/(protected)/tools/nata/page.tsx (directory holds only subfolders) and no app not-found.tsx. localStorage keys qb_onboarding_done / qb_nata_status are global per device.
evidence: question-bank/page.tsx:50, 75, 156 router.push('/tools/nata'); ExamProfileOnboarding.tsx:122-126 sets the global keys then calls onBlocked.
impact: Students who answer 'not interested' land on the default 404. On a shared phone a second account inherits the first account's onboarding answer, including being bounced to the 404.
fix: Redirect to /dashboard (or the planned tools home) and key the cache by user id (qb_onboarding_done:<uid>).
expected: No 404; per-account onboarding.

title: Exam-year content is stale: planner shows only past NATA 2026 sessions, exam centers say 2025
rootCause: Year-specific data and copy are hardcoded in client files.
evidence: nata-2026-schedule.ts:75-85 and isSessionPast: as of 2026-10-01 every Phase 1 and Phase 2 session is past, so ExamPlannerContent renders only disabled 'Past' cards and no plan can be made. exam-centers/page.tsx:426, 698 and layout.tsx:4-20 say NATA 2025. cutoff page.tsx:103-120 getAcademicYear returns nataYear 2026 from September 2026 while students now prepare for NATA 2027, and the rules text hardcodes 2026/2025.
impact: Tools look abandoned during the main prep season; the planner is inert.
fix: Move schedules and year labels to a DB table or a single config served with revalidate (ISR) so staff can roll the year without a deploy; show an 'NATA 2027 dates not announced yet' empty state when all sessions are past.
expected: Current-cycle dates or an honest 'not announced' state.

title: Cutoff mobile 'See Details' is a dead click on steps 1 and 2
rootCause: handleViewDetails scrolls to #results-section, which exists only when activeStep === 2; showResultsMobile state is set but never read.
impact: Tap does nothing on two of three steps (once the bar is visible after the overlap fix).
fix: Set activeStep to 2, then scroll after render (useEffect on a flag); remove unused state.
expected: See Details always lands on the results.

title: Image crop leaks object URLs, fails silently on undecodable images, and Crop has no busy state
rootCause: Unmount cleanup closes over the initial nulls (deps []), so it never revokes. Slider handlers null croppedUrl without revoking. No img.onerror and a silent return for non image/* types. cropAndCompress runs up to 20 toBlob passes with the button enabled.
impact: Memory growth on low-end phones over repeated crops; HEIC or corrupt files (common from Android galleries) do nothing with no message; double taps run two compress loops.
fix: Track URLs in refs and revoke on replace and unmount; add img.onerror with a 'Could not read this image, try a JPG or PNG' message; disable the Crop button with a progress label while processing. Consider drag-to-pan on the preview instead of three sliders.
expected: No leaked blobs, visible errors, single-flight crop.

title: Exam centers: city list and searches can race
rootCause: Cities effect has no cancel flag; Enter in the search field calls searchCenters even while loading (button is disabled, the key handler is not); no AbortController.
impact: Switching state quickly can show the previous state's cities; a second Enter shows whichever search returns last.
fix: Cancelled flag in the cities effect; guard searchCenters on loading or abort the previous request.
expected: Only the latest request writes state.

title: Posting a question gives no confirmation; ?posted=true is ignored and the pending post is invisible
rootCause: new/page.tsx pushes /tools/nata/question-bank?posted=true but the list never reads the param; moderated posts do not appear in the list.
evidence: new/page.tsx:122; question-bank/page.tsx has no useSearchParams.
impact: Students think their post was lost and repost (duplicates for moderators).
fix: Read posted=true and show a Snackbar 'Sent for review, usually within 24 hours', or a 'My pending posts' row.
expected: Clear success feedback.

title: Exam planner phase and session cards are mouse/touch only; error close button does nothing
rootCause: Paper with onClick and no role, tabIndex or key handler; Alert onClose={() => {}}.
evidence: ExamPlannerContent.tsx:69-107 (PhaseToggle), 134-191 (SessionCard), 441.
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot pick phases or sessions; the X on the error alert is a dead control.
fix: Use ButtonBase or role='button' tabIndex=0 with Enter/Space and aria-pressed; wire onClose to clear the error.
expected: Fully keyboard operable.

title: Cutoff page is a 1379-line client component with all input state at page level
rootCause: useCalculatorState lives in the page; every keystroke re-renders all sections, the results panel, InfoSection, and re-stringifies resultData in useScoreAutoSave (effect keyed on a new object each render).
evidence: wc -l: 1379 lines (measured). page.tsx:1088, 1096-1123; useScoreAutoSave.ts:131.
impact: Small today (no heavy children); grows as the page grows. Not a priority on its own.
fix: During the redesign, split sections into files, memoise the static InfoSection, and key autosave on a primitive fingerprint string.
expected: Typing re-renders only the active section and results.

title: SEO metadata on login-gated, client-only tool pages; college-predictor canonical points at a redirect
rootCause: Pages are 'use client' and sit under the client ProtectedLayout, which renders 'Loading...' on the server and nothing until a Firebase user exists, so crawlers never see the 'Free tool' content the layouts advertise. college-predictor/page.tsx redirects to /tools/counseling/college-predictor but its layout sets canonical to the redirecting URL; next.config.js:55 sends /tools/college-predictor through two hops.
evidence: cutoff-calculator/layout.tsx:3-25, exam-centers/layout.tsx:3-25, college-predictor/layout.tsx:3-25 and page.tsx:4; (protected)/layout.tsx:299-311 and 349.
impact: No search value from these pages; a redirect chain for legacy links.
fix: Either drop the marketing metadata here (keep SEO on the marketing site) or move the static explainer to a public server-rendered route; delete the college-predictor layout metadata and point next.config redirects straight to /tools/counseling/*.
risk: Low; coordinate with the SEO agent.
expected: No canonical to a redirect; one-hop redirects.

title: Em dashes in user-visible copy (brand rule)
rootCause: Copy written with U+2014.
evidence: 11 user-visible occurrences (grep): cutoff-calculator/page.tsx:467, 468, 875, 1032, 1148; cutoff-calculator/PurposePrompt.tsx:116, 179; cost-calculator/page.tsx:119; question-bank/new/page.tsx:229; components/exam-planner/ExamPlannerContent.tsx:436; components/question-bank/ContributionPrompt.tsx:42. No user-visible '--'. Comment-only occurrences (not counted): useScoreAutoSave.ts:32-33, question-bank/page.tsx:49.
impact: Copy reads as AI-generated, against CLAUDE.md content rules.
fix: Replace with commas, colons or periods (for example 'Eligible: 72% aggregate (minimum 45% required)').
expected: Zero em dashes in rendered text.

title: Emoji and text glyphs used as icons
rootCause: Emoji/Unicode in place of SVG icons.
evidence: ComingSoonPage.tsx:15-17 4rem emoji (U+1F3DB / U+1F4D0); VoteButton.tsx:89,121 and ImprovementSection.tsx:131 triangle glyphs; question-bank/page.tsx:288 '+' text FAB with no aria-label; [id]/page.tsx:228 and new/page.tsx:136 '←' text arrows. AuthGate.tsx:96,134-136 (shared, unreachable in protected).
impact: Inconsistent rendering across Android/iOS fonts; violates the SVG-icon rule.
fix: Use @mui/icons-material (ArrowUpward/ArrowDownward, Add with aria-label, ArrowBack) and an SVG illustration on ComingSoonPage.
expected: SVG icons only.

title: No consistent tool header or back path; each tool page invents its own
rootCause: No shared ToolPageHeader and no /tools/nata hub inside (protected).
evidence: h4 at fixed 2.125rem (exam-centers:422, image-crop:285, eligibility:248, cost:186); h4 with responsive size (cutoff:1144); icon + h6 with own padding and maxWidth 600 (ExamPlannerContent.tsx:408-416); h5 + inline action (question-bank:164-184); text Back button (QB [id]:216, QB new:135); ComingSoon 'Back to Dashboard' (ComingSoonPage.tsx:28-36). None of the 7 working tools has a back link.
impact: On phones the only way out is the bottom nav or hamburger; header sizes jump between tools.

title: JoSAA predictor re-submits forever after any failed request
rootCause: The 'Re-run after sign-in' effect runs when user && submitted && !predictions && !byYear && !loading, with loading in its deps. handleSubmit clears predictions, sets loading true, and on any failure leaves predictions null and sets loading false in finally. The loading true->false transition re-satisfies the condition, so handleSubmit runs again, indefinitely.
evidence: page.tsx:182-272 handleSubmit (setPredictions(null) at 185, setLoading(false) in finally at 270); page.tsx:275-277 effect deps [user, submitted, predictions, byYear, loading, handleSubmit]. The user is always signed in under (protected), so the guard never stops it. Triggers: rank > 1,500,000 (client only checks >= 1, server returns 400 at route.ts:61-66), any 500, expired token, or offline (fetch rejects immediately, so the loop runs as fast as the device can fail).
impact: A single bad input or network blip turns into a continuous stream of authenticated POSTs (each a firebase verify plus predict_colleges_v2 RPC from iad1 to Singapore), battery drain on phones, the error banner flickering, and function invocation cost.
fix: Delete the re-run effect (the page is under the protected layout, the user always exists) or gate it with a ref that is set once and only cleared on a successful sign-in transition. Also clamp rank on the client to 1..1,500,000.
risk: Low. The effect only existed for the pre-auth AuthGate flow, which cannot happen under (protected).
expected: Exactly one request per Predict tap; failures end in the error Alert.

title: App functions run in iad1 (Washington) while Supabase is in Singapore
rootCause: apps/app/vercel.json sets no regions, so Vercel functions default to iad1. The database is ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) behind the db.neramclasses.com Cloudflare proxy. apps/nexus/vercel.json already pins regions ["sin1"].
evidence: Live responses carry x-vercel-id bom1::iad1::... (edge Mumbai, function Washington) for /api/tools/counseling-insights and /api/tools/rank-predictor. One-query GET /api/tools/counseling-insights took 0.36 to 0.38 s warm and 1.66 s cold from India; the same DB statements average 0.2 to 11 ms in pg_stat_statements, so almost all of the time is transit. Every sequential Supabase call in a handler pays a US to Singapore round trip (roughly 200 ms, not individually measured).
impact: Every tool request is slow for an India-based user base; the counseling predictor (10 to 22 sequential queries) is multiplied by it. Students on 4G see multi-second waits.
fix: Add "regions": ["sin1"] (or bom1 if Supabase is moved later) to apps/app/vercel.json, matching Nexus. Verify after deploy that x-vercel-id shows ::sin1::.
risk: Applies to all app routes. Firebase Admin, Razorpay and Resend are global or India-near, so latency to them does not get worse. Requires a deploy of the app only.
expected: Per-query round trip drops from about 200 ms to tens of ms; counseling college prediction from seconds to well under one second (estimate, not measured).

title: Counseling college prediction makes 10 to 22 sequential DB round trips
rootCause: The handler awaits each step in turn: system lookup (route.ts:58), predictRankFromScore (rank summary view, then a 1 to 3 step 'nearby' loop, then above/below, then a community_rank check, then 1 or 2 category counts, then a 1 to 3 step similar-students loop, or on the allotment path one count query per community in a for loop plus a directory read), then predictCollegesWithSeatAwareness (directory, then COA intake, then get_college_seat_occupancy, then get_college_total_occupancy). Independent steps are not parallelised, and similarStudents is computed although the college predictor page never reads it.
evidence: counseling.ts:507-531 (summary), 535-550 (nearby loop, no limit, used only for a count), 555-566 (above/below), 602-676 (category checks, sequential counts at 655-669), 684-691 (similar students), 432-455 (per-community counts in a loop), 1452 (directory), 1398 (coa), 1455 and 1485 (two RPCs that do not depend on each other). pg_stat_statements: these statements average 0.2 to 11 ms, so DB time is not the problem; the count of round trips is.
impact: With the iad1 to Singapore hop each prediction is several seconds (not measured end to end; needs an auth token). The same chain backs /api/tools/rank-predictor POST.
fix: 1) Pass a flag so the college predictor skips similarStudents. 2) Start directory+COA+total occupancy (rank independent) in Promise.all with predictRankFromScore; run the two occupancy RPCs together; run catCheck alongside above/below. 3) Replace the nearby loop with a count head query. 4) Longer term, one SQL function predict_counseling(system, year, score, category) returning rank + colleges in a single round trip.
risk: Low for steps 1 to 3 (pure reordering); step 4 needs a migration and parity tests on TNEA and KEAM.
expected: About 4 to 5 round trips instead of 10 to 22; with sin1, sub-second responses.

title: Counseling tools open on a system with no data (21 of 23 active systems are empty)
rootCause: getCounselingSystems returns every is_active system ordered by name (counseling.ts:39-52) and each page picks the first active one: 'ACPC Gujarat B.Arch'. Only TNEA_BARCH (rank list 1,399 rows, allotment 3,553, directory 38) and KEAM_BARCH (rank list 1,649, own keam_* tables) have data; the other 21 active systems have zero rows everywhere.

Pages: college-predictor page.tsx:568-571, rank-predictor page.tsx:115-119, insights page.tsx:124-125. Rank predictor then disables the score field with 'Data not available yet, coming soon'; insights shows 'No data available for this counseling system'; college predictor returns 'No colleges found'. user_funnel_events: 8 tool_opened for college_predictor_counseling and 0 tool_completed in 30 days.

Redirects run before the filesystem, so apps/app/src/app/tools/{college-predictor,cutoff-calculator,exam-centers}/page.tsx never render. The targets live under (protected), whose client layout server-renders only 'Loading...'.

title: College predictor fires the prediction twice on the first tap
rootCause: The results are wrapped in <AuthGate hasData={hasSearched} onAuthenticated={handleCounselingPredict}>. Under (protected) the user always exists, so as soon as hasSearched flips true AuthGate's effect (AuthGate.tsx:44-52) schedules onAuthenticated after 100 ms, which calls handleCounselingPredict a second time. The same happens after the URL auto-predict (page.tsx:600-604).
evidence: page.tsx:614 setHasSearched(true) inside the first call; AuthGate.tsx:45 condition user && hasData && onAuthenticated && !hasCalledCallback; page.tsx:943 passes handleCounselingPredict. Neither call checks an in-flight flag, so two heavy POSTs race and the first to finish clears loading while the second is still running.
impact: Doubles the most expensive request in the app on every visit's first prediction and double-counts tool_completed analytics.
fix: Remove AuthGate from the protected counseling pages (college-predictor, josaa-predictor, insights, rank-predictor): it can never show its gate there. At minimum drop onAuthenticated on college-predictor.
risk: Low. AuthGate is only meaningful on public pages.
expected: One POST per Predict tap.

title: counseling-insights GET is never cached although the data is public
rootCause: force-dynamic and no Cache-Control header on any of its three response shapes, unlike /api/tools/rank-predictor which sets s-maxage=3600. With systemId+year it also re-reads both year summary views: getAvailableYearsWithSource (2 views) is awaited first, then getRankListYearSummary and getAllotmentYearSummary are read again inside the Promise.all (CACHE-3), and the client ignores the yearsWithSource it gets back.
evidence: curl: x-vercel-cache MISS on repeated calls; systems list 0.36 to 1.66 s, ?systemId 0.47 to 1.42 s, ?systemId&year 0.64 to 1.30 s. /api/tools/rank-predictor?action=years: MISS 1.85 s then HIT 0.13 s. route.ts:42 then 55-62.
impact: Every insights visit costs three uncached function invocations and about 1.5 to 3 s of waiting; this is the cheapest fix in the set.
fix: Add headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400' } to all three responses; reuse the summaries from getAvailableYearsWithSource instead of fetching them again, and run all five reads in one Promise.all.
risk: Public, non-personal aggregates only. New data appears within an hour.
expected: CDN HIT about 0.13 s, as measured on the rank-predictor GET.

title: Prediction POSTs recompute identical results for identical inputs
rootCause: The outputs depend only on the inputs (system, year, score, category; or JoSAA rank, category, gender, home state, year, round), not on the user, but nothing caches them. Auth is a lead gate, not a per-user data scope.
evidence: pg_stat_statements since 2025-12-19: get_college_seat_occupancy 3,715 calls, predict_colleges_v2 358 calls, counseling_systems select 1,218 calls. getCounselingSystemByCode runs on every POST for a 23-row table that changes rarely.
impact: Repeated function time and DB round trips for scores many students share (whole-number composite scores, common ranks).
fix: Keep the auth check, then wrap the pure computation in unstable_cache keyed by the normalised inputs with revalidate 86400 and a 'counseling-data' tag; cache the system lookup the same way. Keep the response itself private.
risk: Stale results for up to a day after a data import; mitigate with revalidateTag from the import script or admin.
expected: Repeat inputs answer from the data cache with zero DB round trips.

title: Tool usage logging is fire-and-forget and records nothing
rootCause: logToolUsage(...).catch(() => {}) is not awaited and not registered with waitUntil, so on Vercel the function can be frozen as soon as the response is returned. logToolUsage itself does 3 sequential writes (user lookup by Firebase uid, insert, funnel event) from iad1 to Singapore, the slowest kind of work to leave unawaited.
evidence: tool_usage_logs has 0 live rows on prod; user_funnel_events has 8 tool_opened and 0 tool_completed for tool funnels in 30 days, although the admin-client fix (fbd39a45) has been live since 2026-09-27. Cause of the zero is inferred (it could also be no completed predictions, see the default-system finding).
impact: The tool funnel cannot show completions, so product decisions on these tools are blind.
fix: import { waitUntil } from '@vercel/functions' and wrap each logToolUsage call, or await it after the region move makes it cheap. Add one structured log line per request with route, duration and status (no tokens or emails).
expected: tool_usage_logs and tool_completed rows appear for each prediction.

title: Database errors become 'no data' or a wrong rank
rootCause: predictRankFromScore destructures { data } without error for the nearby loop (536), above/below (555-566), community_rank check (602), category above/below (612-627) and both category counts (655-669). If the 'below' query fails while 'above' succeeds, the code takes the 'score is below the entire dataset' branch and returns predictedRank = totalCandidates (worst rank). predictCollegesWithSeatAwareness ignores the total-occupancy RPC error (1485), dropping every closing rank. The route swallows any seat-aware exception (route.ts:195) and falls back to historical_cutoffs, which has 0 rows on prod, returning 200 with null predictions. counseling-insights maps three stats failures to [] (route.ts:59-61).
evidence: Code references above; historical_cutoffs n_live_tup = 0 on prod.
impact: A transient failure tells a student they are last, or shows 'No colleges found', with a 200 status that no log or alert sees.
fix: Check error on every query and throw; in the route, return 503 with a retryable message instead of the legacy fallback (or remove the dead fallback entirely).
risk: Low; turns silent wrong answers into visible, retryable errors.
expected: DB failures surface as 5xx and an error state with Retry.

title: Insights page: stale data under a new year label, swallowed errors, response races
rootCause: All three fetches call res.json() without res.ok and end in .catch(() => {}). Changing year does not clear funnel/colleges, so if the request fails the previous year's numbers stay on screen under 'Overview, {new year}'. Tapping year chips quickly lets an older response land last (no AbortController or request id). A failed systems fetch reads as 'No data available for this counseling system'.
evidence: page.tsx:118-129, 132-145, 148-163; funnel only reset on system change (136).
impact: Students can read wrong-year statistics; failures look like missing data with no Retry.
fix: Use SWR (or AbortController) keyed by systemId+year, check res.ok, clear data on key change, and render an error Alert with a Retry button.
expected: Only the latest selection's data is shown; failures show Retry.

title: Rank and college predictors disable themselves on a transient fetch failure

The rank predictor also keeps community stats from years[0] when the user picks another year, but labels them 'Based on {selectedYear} data' (308-312); the 'Accuracy' card shows a count of nearby students, not accuracy (405-415).

title: JoSAA results default to a 9-column table on phones
rootCause: useState<ViewMode>(isMobile ? 'cards' : 'table') captures the first render, where MUI useMediaQuery returns false (no noSsr), so every device starts in 'table'. The table has 9 columns (702-737) and scrolls sideways inside its Paper at 375px.

title: COA checker search and browse: out-of-order results and errors shown as empty
rootCause: handleSearch writes whatever response arrives, with no request identity, so a slow 'ch' result can replace 'chennai'. BrowseTab refetches on every filter/page change with no abort, and handleStateChange races getCOACities. Errors are caught into [] so the UI says 'No colleges found' or '0 colleges found' with no Retry. The debounce timeout is not cleared on unmount.
impact: Wrong results for the typed query; outages read as 'college not found', which on a COA approval checker can mislead a student about a college's status.
fix: Track a request counter (or AbortController via a route) and ignore stale responses; separate error from empty with a Retry; clear the timer in an effect cleanup.
expected: Results always match the current query; errors are explicit.

title: Tools hub and help page: wrong canonical, legacy links, emoji icons, help behind login

It lists only four NATA-era tools with emoji icons, all linking to 308-redirected URLs, and omits the counseling and JoSAA tools.
